evidence: Performance can degrade when relevant information is placed in the middle of a long input context, even for explicitly long-context models.
use: supports retrieval-first context packing instead of whole-document injection

evidence: Retrieval-augmented models combine parametric memory with a dense vector index and improve specificity and factuality over parametric-only baselines on knowledge-intensive tasks.
use: supports explicit document index and provenance

evidence: Fixed retrieval can be unhelpful; adaptive retrieval and self-reflection improve factuality and citation accuracy.
use: supports sufficiency gating and selective verification

evidence: Late-interaction retrieval represents query and passages at token granularity and improves retrieval quality while controlling storage through compression.
use: supports future reranking/late-interaction adapter rather than relying on one vector

evidence: Long-term conversational evaluation includes hundreds of turns across sessions, and long-context models or RAG still lag human performance on long-range temporal and causal understanding.
use: supports dedicated memory evaluation and rolling summaries

evidence: Long-term agent memory is discussed as separate procedural, semantic, and episodic systems, with memory management remaining an open problem.
use: supports typed memory instead of one prompt block

evidence: Knowledge tracing models student knowledge acquisition from sequences of interactions and build on Bayesian knowledge tracing for learner-state estimation.
use: supports event-based learner state and uncertainty

evidence: Spacing and retrieval practice are reviewed as effective learning strategies across applied educational settings.
use: supports using memory to drive retrieval and spaced review

evidence: A systematic review of classroom studies found retrieval practice improved learning across education levels, content areas, delays, formats, and feedback timings.
use: supports diagnostic retrieval as the primary memory intervention
